column2: You, Agni, who like a fierce archer, like a sharp-horned bull, broke the forts.
We ask for the unceasing hot offering to Agni Vaishvanara, the truthful, lord of the light of truth.
He who has spread this out, crossing the sacrifice's sound, the master releases the seasons.
Agni in his dear abodes is the desire of what has been and will be; the one sovereign shines.
Agni, adorning his own body by ancient birth, the seer has grown through the sage.
I call Agni, grandson of strength, of pure flame, at this well-ordered sacrifice.
You, Agni, great friend, with bright flame, sit with the gods on the grass.
Your strengths have risen, splitting the demons, O stone-bearer; drive away those who contend.
With this might he struck down at the meeting of the chariots, when wealth is set; I praise with a fearless heart.
The vows of this flowing one cannot be assailed; break him who attacks you.
They urge on that exhilaration-dropping bay racer in the rivers, the drop for Indra, joyful.
Devourer of Vritra, breaker of Vala, destroyer of forts, driver of the waters; standing on the chariot of the bay horses, loudly, Indra breaks even the firm.
Like deep oceans you nourish skill, like cattle; like good herdsmen, like cows to fodder, like channels to a lake they reach.
May the drops delight you, bounteous Indra, so that you give wealth to the presser; you drank the soma pressed in the vessels — that eldest strength you hold.
You indeed, O mightiest god, are praised for the mortal; there is no other than you, bounteous one, to be gracious; Indra, I speak this word to you.
Let neither your bounties nor your helps ever harm us, O Vasu; and bring all treasures to us, to the peoples, O Manu.
Facing, the good leader of men, the one who shines around the sister, the daughter of heaven has been seen.
Like a mare, wondrous, ruddy, mother of cows, truthful — Dawn became the friend of the Ashvins.
You are the friend of the Ashvins and the mother of cows; and, O Dawn, you rule over wealth.
This incomparable Dawn dawns, the beloved of heaven; I praise you, Ashvins, loudly.
Who are the wonder-workers, children of the river, swifter than thought of riches, finders of wealth with the gods by thought.
Your humps are spoken of on the old peak, where your chariot flew with the birds.
O Dawn, bring that wondrous thing to us, O rich in strength, by which we may hold children and grandchildren.
O Dawn, today here, rich in cattle and horses, shining one, dawn richly for us, O truthful.
Yoke, O Dawn, the ruddy horses, rich in strength, today; then bring us all good fortunes.
Ashvins, bring your path to us with cattle and gold, wonder-workers; bring your chariot near, of one mind.
Come here, gods, gladdening wonder-workers, golden-pathed; may the dawn-wakers carry you to drink the soma.
You who thus made the praise of heaven's light for the people, Ashvins, bring us strength.
I regard Agni as the one who is wealth, to whom the cows come home; home the swift horses, home the steadfast strong ones; bring food to the singers.
For Agni, all-seeing, gives a racer to the clan; Agni gives wealth, self-existing; pleased, he goes to the choice; bring food to the singers.
He is Agni, the Vasu, who is praised, to whom the cows come together, the swift horses, together the well-born sages; bring food to the singers.
You who dawned for the good leader Shaucadratha, daughter of heaven — dawn, then, upon the more strong, true-famed Vayya, well-born, rich in horses and truth.
Bring us wealth today, Vasu; dawn, daughter of heaven, you who dawned on the stronger, true-famed, well-born, rich in horses and truth.
Your best-loved chariot, the bull, carrier of wealth, O Ashvins — the singer adorns it with hymns; O honeyed ones, hear my call.
Come across all sins, Ashvins, wonder-workers, golden-pathed, bringing happiness, river-carrying; O honeyed ones, hear my call.
Bring us jewels, Ashvins; come, Rudras, golden-pathed, delighted, rich in strength; O honeyed ones, hear my call.
The priest has been awakened to worship the gods; Agni stands high, well-minded, in the morning; of the kindled his shining strength has been seen; the great god is freed from darkness.
When he pulled the girdle of the troop, the pure Agni anoints with pure cows; then the right fire-stick is yoked, striving; standing high, he eats with the ladles the stretched out.
This best light of lights has come; the wondrous banner has been born, pervading; as the night, sent forth by Savitar for his impulse, gave way to the dawn.
The white one has come, calf-bearing, shining; the dark has left her abodes; two immortal kinswomen, following one another, move, changing color, heaven's color.

The path of the two sisters is common and endless; they travel it in turn, taught by the gods; they do not hinder nor stand still, the two good-formed, night and dawn, of one mind, of different forms.
Agni shines, the face of the dawns; the speeches of the sages, godly, have risen; come now here, you two charioteers, to the swollen hot milk, Ashvins.
The two do not break the prepared offering; may they come near, Ashvins, now praised here; at day-time, on the evening, to the giver, the best-bringing, most blessed, the returning.
And come at the milking in the morning of the day, and at midday at the rising of the sun; by day and night with most comfortable help; the drinking of you two has not yet been spread, Ashvins.
These dawns have made a banner; in the eastern half of space they adorn their light; like bold ones preparing weapons, the ruddy cows, the mothers, go forward.
The ruddy rays have flown up in vain; the well-yoked ones yoked the ruddy cows; the dawns made the signs as before; the ruddy ones rested on the shining light.
They sing like women in their works, with one yoking from afar, bringing nourishment for the good doer, the good giver, for the sacrificer who presses every day.
Agni has been awakened; the Sun rises from the earth; Dawn, the moon, has shone with great light; the Ashvins have yoked their chariot to go; the god Savitar has impelled the world apart.
When, Ashvins, you yoke the bull-chariot, sprinkle our kingly power with ghee and honey; strengthen our prayer in battles; may we win wealth in hero-contests.

Let the three-wheeled, honey-carrying chariot of the Ashvins, with swift horses, well praised, come near; three-seated, bounteous, giving all good fortune, may it bring well-being to our two-footed and four-footed.
Your unattached streams go like rains from heaven toward a thousandfold strength.
Looking toward dear poems and all, the bay one flows, pressing weapons.
He, cleansed by the Ayus, a king of good vows, sits in the fleece like a falcon on wealth.
Bring us, O drop, all treasures from heaven and from the earth, purifying.
His streams have flowed forth by the might of the pressed bull, adorning toward the gods.
The ordainers cleanse the horse, the singers praise with song, the light being born, worthy of praise.
Those are easily overcome by you, Soma, flowing, O lord of wealth; strengthen the praiseworthy ocean.
To you, lord of strength, the songs go like restrained ones.
Like streams on paths, may your gifts, Indra, go forth in all directions.
We turn you toward help and favor like a chariot — the strong-acting, helper, bountiful, mightiest Indra, lord of the good.
O of great strength, of great wisdom, rich in power, with all your thought you have filled all by your greatness.
Whose greatness, Indra, the two hands, holding the golden thunderbolt, went around the earth.
Who lit up the fort of the Narmin, the seer in the cloud, like a bright young bull, a sun-like shining one, hundred-souled.
Twice-born, he has stood shining over the three lights and all spaces; the best sacrificing priest in the seat of the waters.
This is the priest who, twice-born, holds all desirable and famous things; to the mortal, good in children, who gives to him.
Agni, today we make you succeed with praises, like a horse, as skill that touches the heart, with our offerings.
Then, Agni, you are the charioteer of auspicious, skilful, effective skill, of the great truth.
With these hymns, be favorable to us, light like heaven; Agni, with all your flames, be kind.
You are a beloved messenger, carrier of offerings, Agni, charioteer of sacrifices; together with the Ashvins and Dawn, give us heroic fame, great.
The gray one swallowed the shaker, the youth, in the gathering of many; see the poem of the god in its greatness — today he is dead, yesterday he lived.
The able one by his power, the ruddy fair-winged, the great hero, ever-dwelling; what he knows is true and not in vain, the desirable treasure, he is both winner and giver.
With these he took the manly powers by which the thunderbolt-bearer slew Vritra; the gods who were born from the work, from the greatness of the work being done, without work.
Mitra, Aryaman and Varuna drink of the extended purified one, of the three-seated, vigorous.
And now Indra enjoys the pressed soma with cattle; he rejoices like the morning priest.
Indeed you are great, O Sun; indeed, O Aditya, you are great; the greatness of you who exist is most to be praised; by might, O god, you are great.
Indeed, Sun, by fame you are great; ever, god, you are great; by greatness the lord-power of the gods, the household priest, all-pervading, unconquerable light.
